instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, the salt and a few grinds of pepper and cook, stirring, until the onion is soft, 5 to 8 minutes.
Peel the squash, scoop out the seeds and cut it into 3/4-inch cubes. Add the squash to the pot and cook, stirring now and then, until it starts to soften, 8 to 10 minutes.
Add the garlic, 2 tsp chopped sage, 1 tsp minced rosemary and 1 tsp grated ginger. Stir for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Pour in 2 cups of the broth and bring it to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes, until the squash is tender.
Let the soup cool for a few minutes. Blend it in batches in a blender, leaving the lid vent open and covered with a towel, until it's completely smooth. An immersion blender works in the pot.
If the soup is too thick, stir in up to 1 cup of the remaining broth.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt and pepper.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top with 2 tbsp chopped parsley and the pepitas.
Leftover soup keeps in the fridge for 4 days. It freezes in portions for up to 3 months. Reheat it over low heat with a splash of water.
method_notes: Lead is Love and Lemons (4.95 from 2,124): onion and squash cooked in oil before any liquid goes in, sage, rosemary and ginger for flavor, then broth and a blend until smooth. Halved for 4. The bread served with it is left out to keep the soup gluten free, and the vegetable broth should be a gluten-free one.
